title: What to Do After a Burst Pipe: The First Hour
description: What to do after a burst pipe: shut off the water, cut power to wet areas, and photograph the damage before cleanup starts.
author: Example Restoration Co.

faqs.question: Should I turn off the electricity after a burst pipe?
faqs.answer: Turn off power to any room where water has reached outlets, cords, or appliances, but only if you can reach the panel without standing in water.

faqs.question: Do I need to photograph the damage before cleanup?
faqs.answer: Yes. Photos of the source, the standing water, and the affected belongings help your insurer understand what happened.

heroImageAlt: Water spreading across a kitchen floor from under a sink cabinet
intro: Shut the water off, make the area safe, then document before anything is moved.
html:
What to Do After a Burst Pipe, Step by Step

The first hour after a burst pipe decides how far the water travels. Find the main shutoff and close it before anything else.

Make the area safe

Cut power to rooms where water has reached outlets or cords. Keep children and pets away from wet floors.

Document Before You Clean

Photograph the source and every wet room. Our water damage restoration crews start from those photos too.

Drying takes longer than it looks; see how long structural drying takes. Wet drywall is its own decision: when to replace wet drywall.

Insurance & What’s Covered

Your policy wording decides what is covered, and your adjuster confirms it. Keep every photo and receipt.
